review_output: {"summary":"Text-only review. The capture's savepoint boundary, DB-clock proof check, immutable/no-truncate guards and replay-based projection are mostly sound. Two MAJOR issues: (1) projection takes locks in the order Version→Live→FormSubmission, the reverse of the existing Live→FormSubmission→Version order, so it can deadlock with Live updates; (2) unlike the earlier metric migration, this one does not revoke privileges from service_role. The NO ACTION FK from capture to visitor matches the existing registration FK and works with parent cascades, because NO ACTION is checked at the end of the statement. But a capture can't be deleted directly, so visitor erasure is permanently blocked; this needs a decision before retention is enabled. Limits: callers, the context resolver, the proof service, verification, reconciliation and Prisma column types were not provided and are not certified. Untested cases noted below are not assumed covered.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"lock ordering","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"materializeMetricRegistration locks Version SHARE before Live and FormSubmission, the reverse of the existing order.","evidence":"materialize locks Version FOR SHARE, then Live FOR SHARE, then FormSubmission FOR SHARE. The registration, session and interval guards lock Live, then FormSubmission, then Version. A Live UPDATE holds the Live row and its source_changed trigger then UPDATEs every LiveMetricVersion row for that live.","impact":"Projection holds Version SHARE and waits for Live, while a Live updater holds Live and waits to update Version: a deadlock. One side aborts; projection becomes PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE and relies on reconciliation. This breaks the stated version-first/source-first lock discipline.","recommended_fix":"In materialize, lock in the guard order (Live, then FormSubmission, then Version) after reading the capture reference. Do the same for any other path that locks Version before Live.","required_test":"Two-connection test: projection pauses after its first lock while a concurrent Live formId/videoId UPDATE runs. Assert there is no 40P01 deadlock and the projection completes or returns a classified state.","confidence":0.8},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"security/privileges","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"service_role is not revoked on the capture table or its functions, unlike the existing metric contract.","evidence":"The earlier migration revokes from anon, authenticated and service_role. This one loops only over anon and authenticated. Default privileges may grant service_role access to new public tables, and service_role bypasses RLS.","impact":"Privilege drift: anyone holding the service_role key could read the submission-to-visitor linkage and insert captures through the Data API, outside the trusted backend role.","recommended_fix":"Add service_role to the revoke loops for the table and both functions, matching the earlier migration.","required_test":"Catalog test: has_table_privilege and has_function_privilege return false for anon, authenticated and service_role.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"consistency/integrity","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The 'first creation transaction only' rule is enforced only by callers, not by the database.","evidence":"The guard only requires the submission to be UNVERIFIED and in scope. Nothing ties the capture to the transaction or time that created the submission. If an earlier capture rolled back to its savepoint, a later call with a current proof can still insert.","impact":"A future or mistaken caller could fill an evidence gap later with present-day attribution, which the code comment explicitly forbids.","recommended_fix":"In the guard, require the submission to have been created in the current transaction or within a tight DB-clock window of capturedAt; otherwise reject.","required_test":"Commit an UNVERIFIED submission with no capture, then attempt a capture in a later transaction. Expect rejection.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"delete/cascade","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The capture-to-visitor FK uses NO ACTION, the same as the registration FK. Cascades work, but visitor erasure is permanently blocked.","evidence":"Deleting a version cascades to visitors, captures and registrations in one statement, and NO ACTION is checked at statement end, so this passes. A direct visitor delete is blocked while a capture exists. A registration can be deleted directly, but the capture DELETE guard allows deletion only when the version or submission is gone. SET NULL would fire the UPDATE guard and fail as 'immutable'.","impact":"A single visitor can only be erased by deleting the whole version or the submission. This is acceptable today because retention is off, but it is a blocker for any visitor-level retention or erasure policy.","recommended_fix":"Document version or submission deletion as the only erasure path, or add a controlled erasure function that the guard allows. Decide before enabling retention.","required_test":"Delete Version, Live and FormSubmission with captures and visitors present: all succeed. A direct visitor delete fails with 23503. A direct capture delete fails with 23514.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"consistency","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"The capture guard does not require read committed isolation, unlike every other metric write guard.","evidence":"Other guards raise an error unless transaction_isolation is read committed. The capture runs inside the caller's business transaction, whose isolation level was not provided.","impact":"Under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE, the snapshot-based collection check and the FOR SHARE behaviour differ from what was tested, and serialization failures may surface at commit, outside the savepoint.","recommended_fix":"Enforce read committed or document the required isolation level, and assert it at the capture boundary.","required_test":"Capture inside a SERIALIZABLE outer transaction. Expect a defined result: rejected and reported unavailable.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"consistency/timestamps","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-capture.ts","issue":"Projection ignores collectionEnabled when verification happens.","evidence":"The eligibility check covers scope, verification status, clock order, expiry and pending clock, but not v.collectionEnabled. Collection can be turned off after capture while visitor and session writes are rejected.","impact":"Registrations verified while collection was off are counted, but matching visit and session evidence is not, so report denominators are skewed.","recommended_fix":"Define the policy explicitly: either classify these as a terminal 'collection_disabled' state or document that capture-time eligibility wins.","required_test":"Capture, disable collection, verify, then project. Assert the documented outcome.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"NIT","area":"schema hygiene","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015100000_live_metric_registration_capture/migration.sql","issue":"Redundant index and an ON UPDATE action that differs from the registration FK.","evidence":"scope_submission_idx duplicates what the submissionId primary key already provides. The capture's visitor FK uses ON UPDATE NO ACTION while the registration's uses CASCADE; this is harmless because scope is immutable.","impact":"Extra write cost and small inconsistencies.","recommended_fix":"Drop the redundant index unless a query needs it, and align the ON UPDATE actions.","required_test":"EXPLAIN the reconciliation queries to confirm the primary-key and visitor indexes are used.","confidence":0.6}]}
